description: Benchmark task (docs/benchmark_rules.md). Fully differential gain-boosted folded-cascode amplifier with CMFB and N-/P-input auxiliary amplifiers (Sarkar, Ghosh, Chatterjee, IEEE ISIE 2021, Figs. 1/3/5), gpdk180, 1.8 V. Conditions: nominal (TT 27 C) plus the paper's Table IV process corners SS/FF/FS/SF (gain, UGF, phase margin, power). Targets are the paper's printed values with the 10 % tolerance. No Monte Carlo (the paper reports none). No objective.

source.title: Sarkar, Ghosh, Chatterjee: Design of a 2 mW Power, 112 dB Gain-Boosted, Folded Cascode Amplifier in 0.18 um Process (IEEE ISIE 2021)
source.figure: Fig. 1 (p. 1, main PMOS-input folded cascode with CMFB and the N-input / P-input auxiliary amplifiers), Fig. 3 (P-input auxiliary), Fig. 5 (N-input auxiliary)

supply_V.provenance: paper: abstract / Sec. I 'based on the 0.18 um, 1.8 V CMOS process' (Table III prints +1/-1 V: INCONSISTENT with the abstract and with the 1.8 V gpdk180 rating; 1.8 V single supply used, G6 step 2)

input_common_mode_V.provenance: benchmark_default_unreviewed (curator choice, paper silent): input common mode of the follower transient and of the quiescent-point fixture, inside the PMOS input pair's range (the pair works from ground to ~1 V); the open-loop AC fixtures take the input common mode from the amplifier's own output common mode (~0.95 V at the reference design)

output_common_mode_V.provenance: benchmark_default_unreviewed (curator choice, paper silent): VCM reference of the CMFB (Mp8/Mp9 gates); the CMFB is not a balanced comparator (the output CM sits ~0.14 V below VCM at the reference design: ~0.95 V)

load_capacitance_F.provenance: curator choice from the paper's own FOM: the paper never states CL, but Table III FOM1 = Ai x GBW x CL / Power = 122 (units of its ref. [13]: kV/V.MHz.pF/uW) with Ai = 112.56 dB = 427 kV/V, GBW = 616 MHz and P = 2.083 mW gives CL = 122 x 2083 / (427 x 616) = 0.97 pF, so 1 pF per output to ground (the family default) is used

constraints.name: input_noise_V_per_rtHz
constraints.aggregate: worst case over all conditions and matching points
constraints.provenance: paper: ISIE 2021 (Sarkar et al.) p. 3 text: simulated equivalent input noise density 4.1 nV/rtHz 'as per Fig. 10' (Fig. 10: flat 4.088 nV/rtHz from 1 Hz to beyond 10 MHz, marker at 10 Hz); the calculated 3.8 (Eq. 9) and Table III's 4.68 contradict the figure/text and are not used (INCONSISTENT, G6 steps 2-3). Measured as the spot density at 10 MHz, input-referred to the differential input, open loop: the gpdk180 models carry flicker noise (the reference amplifier shows 1.2 uV/rtHz at 10 Hz, white floor from ~10 MHz) while the paper's curve is flat down to 1 Hz, so the paper's marker frequency (10 Hz) cannot be reproduced in this PDK; 10 MHz lies inside the paper's flat band

constraints.name: slew_rate_pos_V_per_s

constraints.provenance: paper: ISIE 2021 (Sarkar et al.) Table III (p. 4): SR+ 44 V/us (test setup not stated; measured as the 20-80 % slew of the differential output in the Sec. VI 0.5 V step follower fixture, rising edge; the printed value is far below what the paper's own Fig. 12 edge implies, so it is a loose lower bound)

constraints.provenance: paper: ISIE 2021 (Sarkar et al.) Table III (p. 4): SR- 36 V/us (same setup note as SR+; falling edge)
